extracted.intended_audience: NeurIPS/ML conference paper authors, peer-review researchers, conference organizers, and developers of LLM-assisted submission tools
extracted.subtask_description: Validating and improving conference paper submissions by checking authors' Yes/No/NA checklist responses and justifications against the NeurIPS 2024 Author Checklist, using an LLM-based assistant; includes guidance for what authors must provide and how an automated assistant should evaluate and report issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Do the main claims made in the abstract and introduction accurately reflect the paper’s contributions and scope?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must ensure consistency and precision between abstract/introduction and claimed contributions; justifications should point to where claims are stated and to supporting results (including appendices if appropriate). LLM reviewers were observed to comment on matching the abstract and introduction and referencing appendices. Actionable feedback includes recommending precise phrasing, scope limits, and explicit links from claims to evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the paper discuss the limitations of the work performed by the authors?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should explicitly discuss limitations and trade-offs of their approach; LLM feedback often asked for clearer limitation sections and for stating caveats that affect interpretation and generality. Include concrete limitations and potential failure modes, and reference them in the justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theory Assumptions and Proofs
rubrics_metrics.description: For each theoretical result, does the paper provide the full set of assumptions and a complete (and correct) proof?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the paper contains theoretical results, the justification must include the full assumptions and complete, correct proofs. In examples, the assistant checked for presence/absence of theory (NA if none) but recommended that authors still clearly outline assumptions behind statistical models and analyses. For mathematical/theory papers, authors should ensure proofs are complete and pointed to explicitly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental Result Reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the paper fully disclose all the information needed to reproduce the main experimental results of the paper to the extent that it affects the main claims and/or conclusions of the paper (regardless of whether the code and data are provided or not)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must disclose all information affecting reproducibility (data splits, preprocessing, training details, random seeds, hyperparameter selection procedures). LLM reviewers flagged missing reproducibility details and suggested concrete items to add. Reproducibility guidance also recommends pointing to appendices or code releases where full details live.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open access to data and code
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the paper provide open access to the data and code, with sufficient instructions to faithfully reproduce the main experimental results, as described in supplemental material?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should provide accessible code/data and clear instructions for reproducing results (installation, run scripts, dataset fetch instructions). LLM reviews checked for presence of repos/links and asked for explicit instructions; external links given by authors were ignored by the assistant in this deployment, so authors should also document access information within the submission/appendices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental Setting/Details
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the paper specify all the training and test details (e.g., data splits, hyperparameters, how they were chosen, type of optimizer, etc.) necessary to understand the results?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include detailed training/testing setups: dataset splits, preprocessing, hyperparameter values and tuning procedures, optimizer type and settings, evaluation protocols. LLM feedback often listed granular items (optimizer config, implementation availability, non-traditional experiments) as actionable points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experiment Statistical Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the paper report error bars suitably and correctly defined or other appropriate information about the statistical significance of the experiments?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should report error bars/confidence intervals or other correct measures of variability and describe how they were computed (number of seeds, bootstrap procedures, hypothesis tests). LLM reviewers checked correctness of error bar reporting and suggested fixes when definitions were unclear or absent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experiments Compute Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: For each experiment, does the paper provide sufficient information on the computer resources (type of compute workers, memory, time of execution) needed to reproduce the experiments?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report compute type (GPUs/CPUs and model sizes), memory, wall-clock or training hours, and any special hardware or distributed setup. LLM feedback often required more explicit compute/execution time details to assess reproducibility and feasibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code Of Ethics
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the research conducted in the paper conform, in every respect, with the NeurIPS Code of Ethics https://neurips.cc/public/EthicsGuidelines ?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must ensure ethical compliance and reference adherence to the NeurIPS Code of Ethics; LLMs sometimes raised related concerns (e.g., reproducibility issues brought up in ethics answers). Where relevant, authors should point to sections describing ethics-related decisions and safeguards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broader Impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the paper discuss both potential positive societal impacts and negative societal impacts of the work performed?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must explicitly discuss both positive and negative societal impacts; LLM reviewers flagged cases where only positives were discussed and recommended explicitly identifying potential negative impacts, mitigation strategies, references to related work on impact, and where to find the discussion in the paper. Contributions section should demarcate societal impacts clearly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safeguards
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the paper describe safeguards that have been put in place for responsible release of data or models that have a high risk for misuse (e.g., pretrained language models, image generators, or scraped datasets)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond licensing, authors should describe concrete safeguards (access controls, usage restrictions, monitoring, recommended ethical use) and reference sections/appendices containing these details. LLM reviews recommended expanding discussion beyond licensing to active safeguards and guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licenses for existing assets
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the creators or original owners of assets (e.g., code, data, models), used in the paper, properly credited and are the license and terms of use explicitly mentioned and properly respected?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must credit creators and list licenses/terms of use, ideally pointing to exact sections/appendices. LLM reviewers asked for explicit citations and links to license texts and recommended verifying license compatibility across aggregated assets.

rubrics_metrics.name: New Assets
rubrics_metrics.description: Are new assets introduced in the paper well documented and is the documentation provided alongside the assets?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New datasets/models must have accompanying documentation (datasheets/metadata), instructions for usage, website/repository access details, and explicit references in the paper; LLM reviews requested clear pointers to appendices and examples of recommended usage and documentation completeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crowdsourcing and Research with Human Subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: For crowdsourcing experiments and research with human subjects, does the paper include the full text of instructions given to participants and screenshots, if applicable, as well as details about compensation (if any)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicable, include full participant instructions, screenshots, compensation details, and explicit statements about consent procedures. If NA, justify why (e.g., no crowdsourcing or human subjects). LLM reviewers accepted NA when supported by paper content but recommended explicit clarifications about dataset origins and that no human subjects were involved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional Review Board (IRB) Approvals or Equivalent
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the paper describe potential risks incurred by study participants, whether such risks were disclosed to the subjects, and whether Institutional Review Board (IRB) approvals (or an equivalent approval/review based on the requirements of your country or institution) were obtained?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If human subjects are involved, report risks, disclosures, and IRB approvals (or equivalents). If N/A, state why and, where relevant, document licensing and privacy handling for datasets that may include identifiable information. LLM reviewers recommended strengthening statements about data handling and future plans involving human subjects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author answer format and justification requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must answer each checklist question with Yes, No, NA (or TODO) and provide a justification for their answer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justifications should point to specific sections or appendices, be concrete and refer to evidence in the paper. Examples showed that vague references to 'appendices' are insufficient; authors should name the appendix section or page. The assistant ignored external links in this deployment, so in-paper pointers are important. If claiming NA, justify why (e.g., no theory present).

rubrics_metrics.name: LLM Assistant scoring protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: LLM should assign Score=1 for no issues, Score=0.5 for minor improvements, and Score=0 for critical issues (and return the score on a separate line at the end of the review).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical deployment combined 0 and 0.5 into a single 'Needs improvement' category (orange) and used green for no concerns. Prompt guidance included 'use 0 score sparingly'; ensure score appears on a separate line to avoid mixing with textual review. Visual presentation used green/orange/red; authors were encouraged to treat orange feedback carefully and make revisions accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: LLM review style and prompt engineering guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: LLM must be given clear, step-by-step instructions: context (NeurIPS), main goal (assist author on checklist question), inputs (question, author answer and justification, guidelines, paper content), and output (itemized, actionable feedback and a separate score).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective prompts set context, asked the LLM to identify discrepancies between justification and paper, provide examples for Yes/No/NA responses, itemize actionable suggestions, and focus on significant improvements. Earlier iterations mixed score and review; resolved by instructing the score on its own line. For long papers (>35 pages/15k words), only first 15k words were processed with a warning to authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feedback quality and granularity standard
rubrics_metrics.description: The assistant should provide itemized, actionable feedback with concrete points (typically 4–6 distinct points per checklist question) and avoid overly generic or verbose boilerplate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observed good behavior: per-question feedback often contained 4–6 granular suggestions (e.g., optimizer settings, explicit mention of non-traditional experiments). Anti-patterns: generic comments, excessive strictness, ignoring figures (non-multimodal), verbosity. Prompt instructions included 'provide itemized, actionable feedback' and 'focus on significant improvements.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency and variability checks for LLM outputs
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether LLM output variation across multiple runs on the same input is smaller than variation across different papers (sanity check for consistency).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The study tested variance within and across runs and found lower within-paper variance for all but one question (ethics). Use permutation tests and report p-values (e.g., p<0.05 after BH correction) to assess consistency. Also monitor cases where feedback changes across unchanged submissions as an issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation and UI decisions for conveyed feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Format LLM outputs for authors with clear coloring and structure (green = no significant concerns, orange = needs improvement, red = critical issues) and compile per-question responses into a readable HTML report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors were encouraged to carefully review orange feedback. The deployment combined 0 and 0.5 into one 'needs improvement' signal; consider whether differentiating severity is useful or harmful given LLM tendencies to be harsh.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on inputs and multimodality constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: When processing papers, handle only the first 15,000 words for papers longer than ~35 pages; the assistant in this deployment is text-only and ignores figures/other modalities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notify authors when truncation occurs. Anti-pattern: relying on LLM to interpret figures or content outside processed text; plan for multimodal handling if figures are critical. Parsing often failed on ligatures and special characters, so validate PDF-to-text conversion quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parser and document formatting robustness
rubrics_metrics.description: PDF-to-text parsing must correctly handle subsections/titles, spacing in checklists, special characters (ligatures like 'fi'/'fl'), and incomplete checklists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deployment encountered parsing issues requiring code fixes. Ensure checklist extraction is robust to spacing/formatting variations and that the parser detects TODO/NA answers. Also ensure external links are not relied upon for verification (assistant ignored them).

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality, consent, and IRB considerations for deployments
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain anonymity and confidentiality of submitted papers and LLM outputs; obtain informed consent from participants and IRB approval for studies involving participants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this study, submissions were optional, authors could register anonymously, outputs were kept confidential and not shared with reviewers, and the study had CMU IRB approval. When sending papers to third-party LLM APIs, treat data under the API's confidentiality terms and inform participants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation via author perception surveys
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess author perceptions using pre- and post-usage surveys with four Likert-scale questions (lead me to modify my paper; be accurate; include useful suggestions; excited about LLM assistance) plus freeform feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare pre/post responses, use binomial/permutation tests with multiple-testing correction (Benjamini–Hochberg) to determine significance. Collect freeform feedback to categorize issues (inaccuracy, too strict, infeasible changes due to page limits, too generic, capability limits, inconsistency, desire for full paper review, bad at theory, verbosity).

rubrics_metrics.name: Measured usage metrics and thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: Quantify number of 'needs improvement' signals per submission and analyze submission patterns (e.g., repeated submissions, lengthening of justifications after feedback).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the study all submissions received 8–13 'Needs improvement' ratings out of 15; track changes across resubmissions (e.g., increases in justification length) as evidence authors acted on feedback. Use these metrics to infer potential impact but avoid strong causal claims without controlled experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Robustness to adversarial manipulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess (and mitigate) vulnerability of the assistant to gaming via AI-assisted rewriting of justifications that can make the assistant more lenient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The study found the assistant could be manipulated to enhance scores via fabricated justifications. As a rubric, require checks for fabricated content, cross-validation against paper text, and safeguards such as spot-checks by humans or verification procedures for justifications to prevent gaming.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting and transparency of assistant limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Document and report assistant limitations (accuracy failure modes, strictness, inability to handle multimodal content, page-limit truncation) so authors can interpret feedback appropriately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study authors logged common issues (20 reports of inaccuracy, 14 of excessive strictness, others). As a best practice, include warnings to users about known limitations and recommended follow-up (e.g., manual checks).
